assignment:
Your principal is considering changing school policy so that students may not participate in sports or other activities unless they have at least a grade B average. Many students have a grade C average. 
She would like to hear the students' views on this possible policy change. Write a letter to your principal arguing for or against requiring at least a grade B average to participate in sports or other activities. Be sure to support your arguments with specific reasons.
essay_1:
Dear Principal,

I dont think you should make the rule that students need a B average to play sports or do activities. I get that you want kids to try harder in school but I think this rule would hurt the kids its supposed to help.

First, alot of kids at our school have a C average and a C is still passing. Those kids are doing there work. If you take away the thing that makes them want to come to school they might care even less about grades, not more. For some kids practice after school is the only reason they want to get up in the morning. My friend is like that and if he couldnt play basketball I honestly dont know if he would come.

Second, sports and clubs teach you stuff that isnt on your report card. When your on the soccer team or in drama club you learn how to work with other people and be responsible and how to lose without getting mad. You also have to manage your time because you have homework and practice on the same night. You need those things for a job someday and just for life. A kid with a C needs them just as much as a kid with an A, maybe even more.

Third, coaches and club advisors actually care about the students. Alot of times a coach is the one who notices when a kid is having a hard time and tells them to go get help. If you kick those kids off the team they lose that person to.

Instead of a B rule I think you should keep the C rule and start a tutoring program for players whos grades start dropping. That way kids can still play and get help so there grades go up. Some of the older players could even be the tutors.

Thank you for asking what students think. I hope you let every student who is passing keep doing there activities.

Sincerely,
A Concerned Student
essay_2:
Dear Principal,

I am writing about the plan to make students have a B average to play sports or join activities. I think this rule is a mistake. I know you want kids to work harder in class. Still, I think this rule would hurt the same students it is supposed to help.

First, a lot of students at our school have a C average, and a C is a passing grade. Those students do their work and meet the standard. If you take away the one thing that keeps them coming to school, they might stop trying in their classes. For a lot of kids, practice after school is the reason they get out of bed in the morning. Without it, school would feel like a chore.

Second, sports and clubs teach things that a report card does not show. On the soccer team or in drama club, students learn teamwork and responsibility. They learn how to deal with losing a game or messing up a line. They also have to manage their time because they have homework and practice on the same night. These skills matter for jobs later, and a kid with a C needs them as much as a kid with an A.

Third, activities give students adults who pay attention to them. A coach or club advisor can tell when a student is struggling and push them to get help. If we kick those students off the team, we also cut them off from that help. That would leave them alone with their problems, and nobody would notice.

My idea is to keep the C average rule and add a tutoring program for players whose grades drop. That way students can stay on the team while they work on their grades. Kids would not be punished for a bad quarter.

Thank you for asking what we think. I am worried that if this rule passes, a lot of kids will lose the one part of school they care about, and some of them will fall further behind and fail.

Sincerely,
A Concerned Student
